evidence: The hunk shows the long directive printf in the trace_ref_file branch and the reviewer says the fallback branch carries the identical string, so the duplication is real. The thread has no reply but is resolved and outdated across 3 commits; the packet does not show whether a later commit deduplicated it.
guidance_note: When a message string grows long enough to carry policy, define it once and reference it from every branch that prints it before opening the PR.

evidence: The PR's whole purpose is the AGENT DIRECTIVE text, and the reviewer states the existing test asserts only the generic 'hook-triggered lit sync push failed' substring, so the new behavior was untested. No reply; the outdated flag leaves open whether a later commit added the assertion.
guidance_note: When a PR's purpose is a new marker in output, add a test asserting that marker in the same commit.

narrative: Small hook-text change; Copilot raised a duplication and a missing-test finding. Neither thread got a reply, though both were resolved and are outdated, so the packet cannot show whether they were addressed in the later commits.
guidance_observations: Threads resolved without any reply leave no record of whether the finding was fixed or dismissed.

evidence: The hunk shows reconnect() calling s.db.Close() before sql.Open, so a failed reopen leaves the Store holding a closed handle. The agent closed the PR 8 minutes later to recut it as #67 without carrying the fix forward, and Copilot raised the identical finding again as #67/F3.
guidance_note: When recutting a PR, apply or explicitly carry over every open finding on the superseded PR before the new one is reviewed.

narrative: Superseded by #67 within minutes of its single review. Its only finding, close-before-open in reconnect(), was not folded into the recut and reappeared as #67/F3, which cost a duplicate finding there.
guidance_observations: A recut PR should inherit the open findings of the PR it supersedes; here a known bug was re-submitted for review unchanged.

evidence: The hunk shows SyncPush calling SyncCompact (one runSyncMutation) and then a second runSyncMutation for PUSH, so another mutation can take the lock in between. The agent kept the diagnosis and extracted compactWithinLock, using callIntProcedure instead of the suggested raw ExecContext to match the other DOLT_* calls.
guidance_note: When a new step must happen immediately before an existing locked operation, put it inside that operation's lock closure instead of calling a separately locked wrapper.

evidence: The test opened a Store and closed it only on the success path; t.Fatalf runs defers, so defer st.Close() right after Open covers the failure paths. The agent cited the same pattern in TestSyncRemoteLifecycle.
guidance_note: Register cleanup (defer or t.Cleanup) on the line after every Open in a test, as the neighboring tests already do.

evidence: reconnect() closed s.db before sql.Open, so a failed reopen left a closed handle; open-swap-close fixes that. The premise is overstated, though: reconnect's own doc comment says GC already invalidates the old connection ('this connection can no longer be used'), so keeping it is less useful than the reviewer implies. This is the same finding as #66/F1, re-raised because the recut did not carry it over.
guidance_note: Before recutting a PR, apply the findings already raised on the superseded one; this was the second time Copilot raised close-before-open.

narrative: Recut of #66. Three findings, all accepted and fixed in one commit, d170cde. F3 duplicates #66/F1, which the agent could have fixed before re-submitting.
guidance_observations: The recut carried a known open finding from #66 into review unchanged.

evidence: The diff removes the legacy-marker branch, so a hook with only '# links-hook: pre-push v1' now goes through upsertManagedSection, which appends a section after any existing exit, as the reviewer says. The packet does not show whether any v1-marker hooks still exist; if the removal was deliberate, the thread needed a reply saying so, and it got none before merge.
guidance_note: When deleting a migration path, state in the PR which installed states can no longer be upgraded and why that is acceptable, or keep a loud refusal for them.

narrative: Removes legacy pre-push hook handling. The single finding, that v1-marker hooks would now get an appended and possibly unreachable section, was resolved without a reply and the PR merged.
guidance_observations: A real behavior change for existing installs was resolved silently; a one-line reply would have recorded whether that was intended.

evidence: planEject stats the path and writeEject later calls os.WriteFile, which overwrites, so the non-force no-overwrite promise has a TOCTOU gap. The window is small in a one-shot CLI writing to the user's own config dir, so the risk is overstated. O_CREATE|O_EXCL is a one-line fix that makes the contract true, and the thread got no reply.
guidance_note: When a mode promises not to overwrite, have the write itself enforce that (O_EXCL) instead of relying on an earlier stat.

evidence: The hunk treats *eject == "" as 'flag absent', so --eject= is silently ignored and also makes --force error out. The thread has no reply, but it is outdated, and the follow-up #71 is titled 'pflag.Changed proxy' and adds Changed to the flag wrapper, which is the reviewer's fix.
guidance_note: For optional-value flags, check whether the flag was passed with Changed() rather than comparing the value to a sentinel that a user can also type.

narrative: Introduces opt-in template overrides and quickstart --eject. Neither finding got a reply. F2 was addressed through the Changed() proxy that #71 carries; F1's TOCTOU is not addressed anywhere in the packets.
guidance_observations: Findings were addressed or dropped without replies, so the thread does not record which happened.

evidence: The ejectTemplates doc called the operation atomic, but a later writeEject failure leaves earlier files written. The reviewer offered softening the comment as one fix; the agent did that in b9215ac and declined temp-file-and-rollback as over-engineering for a config eject.
guidance_note: Write 'atomic' in a comment only after checking what happens when the write phase fails partway, not only the plan phase.

evidence: The hunk shows this PR deleting an existing isValidTemplateBytes check (non-empty, utf8.Valid, no NUL), yet the agent called the check 'speculative validation for a scenario that doesn't happen'. The pushback never mentions that the PR removed the check, and the packet does not show which path used to call it, so whether dropping it was a regression cannot be settled.
guidance_note: When a refactor deletes a validation, say in the PR why it is no longer needed, so a later reviewer asking for it gets an answer grounded in the deletion rather than 'can't happen'.

evidence: The README line has 'work.  Inspired', a double space; it was collapsed in b9215ac.

Cobra shows a root command's Short only when Long is empty or when the command is listed as a subcommand; the root here sets Long with the tagline, so help output is not blank. The agent also says the owner asked for Short to be removed, which the packet cannot confirm, but the technical rebuttal holds on its own.
planEject set Changed=true before any write, so a failed write still reported a change. b9215ac moved setting Changed into writeEject after a successful os.WriteFile.
guidance_note: Set a result field that reports an effect only after the effect has happened.

narrative: Re-lands the #70 eject work along with the Changed() proxy. Three findings were fixed in b9215ac. The Short pushback was sound. The pushback on override-content validation did not acknowledge that this same PR deleted an existing validation.
guidance_observations: Pushback replies should engage with what the diff itself removed, not argue from first principles that the check was never needed.

evidence: newBlockerAnnotator and enrichWithParentEpic each called GetIssueDetail per row, so 2N fetches. The agent first declined, correctly noting that the suggested code would not compile (no GetParent method, and the cache never hits), then reversed and landed a single fetchIssueDetails pre-pass in a17a153.
guidance_note: Before adding a second per-row fetch of the same data, check whether the pipeline already fetches it and share that result.

evidence: ParentEpic does not affect sortByReadiness, so enriching before applyLimit wasted fetches on rows that get discarded. The enrichment was moved after applyLimit in 377aa10.
guidance_note: Place per-row enrichment that does not affect ordering after the limit is applied.

narrative: Adds the parent epic to ready rows. Both efficiency findings were real. The agent first deferred the duplicate-fetch refactor, then did it the same day, ending with one fetch pass shared by both annotators.
guidance_observations: The agent's initial 'out of scope' deferral was reversed within minutes; with two concrete callers already present, the refactor was in scope from the start.

evidence: strings.Contains(out, "should appear") would pass even if newlines were collapsed, so the test was weak. The agent deleted all of show_test.go, citing a project rule against locking CLI text format. The packet cannot confirm that rule, and the deletion also removed the parent-before-description ordering and no-parent omission checks.
guidance_note: If the project does not test CLI text format, do not add format-asserting tests in the first place; check that convention before writing them.

evidence: strings.Split on a string ending in \n yields a final empty element that becomes a whitespace-only line. The caller adds its own trailing newline, so trimming trailing newlines before splitting (bf9f239) is simpler than the suggested two-branch version and gives the same output.
guidance_note: When writing a line-splitting helper, test it on input with a trailing newline.

narrative: Inlines the parent description in lit show. The indent bug was fixed more simply than suggested. The weak-test finding was resolved by deleting the whole test file, based on a project convention the packet cannot verify.
guidance_observations: Tests written against a convention the agent later invoked to delete them suggest the convention was not checked when writing them.

evidence: getIssueRaw already attaches labels per child, so the trailing attachLabels in GetEpicDetail repeats the work. The reviewer's suggestion block deletes that call, and the reply (posted as elton-prawn) plans exactly that. No fix commit landed, because the PR was closed as superseded by #77.
guidance_note: Before adding a bulk post-pass, check what the per-row fetch it follows already attaches.

evidence: fmt.Errorf("cannot %s %s", in.Action, ...) produces 'cannot done <id>'. The planned fixed wording 'cannot transition epic %s' resolves it without depending on the action token. It was never committed, because the PR was superseded.
guidance_note: Read error templates aloud with each value the action token can take before committing them.

evidence: PeekIssueType returns NotFoundError{Entity:"record"} while the rest of the store uses "issue", so users would see 'record ... not found'. The plan to use "issue" and wrap the other error was not committed before the PR closed.
guidance_note: When adding a store accessor, copy the not-found entity name and error wrapping from its sibling accessors.

evidence: The hunk changes RankToTop's existence check from GetIssue to getIssueRaw, so epic IDs pass and get ranked, and then the CLI's follow-up GetIssue rejects them, leaving a mutation applied with an error reported. This was the most consequential finding on the PR and the only one with no reply.
guidance_note: When widening a validation check from a leaf-only accessor to a raw one, trace every caller that re-reads through the leaf-only accessor afterward.

narrative: Distinct Epic type attempt, closed in favor of #77. Replies came from the account elton-prawn, which also posted three later zero-finding rounds. Three findings got plans, none committed; the rank partial-success finding got no reply at all.
guidance_observations: Replies said 'Applying' on a PR that was then closed without the commits, so the threads record work that never happened.

evidence: The agent shows that statusForStorage returns an invented 'open' for epics, so the suggestion would write a state the epic does not have. Empty from/to on container history matches the PR's model that epics own no status, and #79 then makes that column NULL for containers.

reflect.DeepEqual treats nil and []string{} as different, so the projection could report spurious merge diffs. append([]string{}, labels...) always yields a non-nil slice, and 2174296 adds a regression test.
guidance_note: When switching an equality check to reflect.DeepEqual, normalize nil versus empty for every slice field in the compared struct.

narrative: Large lifecycle-as-expression refactor with only two findings. The pushback on writing a status into container history is well argued and supported by the code. The nil-versus-empty labels fix came with a regression test.

evidence: The docstring says 'open status' but the predicate only skipped in_progress and blocked rows. As the agent notes, the upstream filter limits inputs to open|in_progress, so no bug exists today; 99b8609 states the predicate positively against StateOpen.
guidance_note: Write the predicate the docstring describes rather than its complement under current upstream filtering.

evidence: The test accepted either the blocker or the clear leaf, so it would pass if ordering regressed; the blocker is deterministically first by rank. Tightened to an exact match in 99b8609.
guidance_note: When ordering is deterministic, assert the exact expected item rather than a set of acceptable ones.

narrative: Adds lit next. Two small findings, both accepted and fixed in one commit within minutes.

evidence: Changing an epic to a leaf leaves the AllOf lifecycle in place, so statusForStorage writes '' and the CHECK fails. The agent rejected the suggested 'empty means open' default and instead refused container-leaf type changes in UpdateIssue, which was the reviewer's option (a); 8af82da adds that guard and a test.
guidance_note: When a type field selects the shape of another field, decide in the same PR whether updates may change the type, and guard it.

evidence: CREATE TABLE embedded the CHECK clause inline while canonicalStatusCheckClause also existed, so the claim of a single definition was false. In 8af82da, createIssuesTableStmt builds CREATE TABLE from the shared const with fmt.Sprintf.
guidance_note: When introducing a shared constant, replace every inline copy of it in the same commit.

evidence: The agent verified that reopening created no extra commit on the current Dolt, so the predicted migration storm did not happen and the risk is only to future versions. The fix's two-way strings.Contains is looser than stripping outer parentheses: any constraint that contains the canonical clause as a substring would also pass. The new TestMigrationIsIdempotentOnSecondOpen does pin the real effect.
guidance_note: When tolerating format differences, normalize the specific difference (outer parentheses) rather than switching to substring matching.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: 8af82da only moved canonicalStatusCheckClause, and the round-0 hunk shows the same inline CHECK text before review, so the NULL gap predates the fix. A leaf row with status NULL makes the OR evaluate to NULL, which a CHECK treats as passing; 6e87c5b adds IS NOT NULL and a raw-insert test.
guidance_note: When a CHECK constraint is meant to reject NULL, include IS NOT NULL explicitly and add a test that inserts NULL directly.

narrative: Makes container status NULL and enforces it with a CHECK. Round 0's three findings were fixed in 8af82da. The F1 response refused container-leaf type changes rather than reintroducing an invented default. Round 1's NULL-passes-CHECK finding is on text 8af82da only moved, so it is a pre-existing gap, not caused by a fix.
guidance_observations: The schema-level invariant was claimed before it was tested against NULL; a raw-insert test for each forbidden shape would have caught F4 before review.

evidence: The reviewer cites lifecycle.go showing Progress() counts leaf descendants, so labeling it 'children:' can disagree with the direct-children list when sub-epics exist. The PR merged at 11:45:12, before the review arrived at 11:46:33, and the thread is unresolved.
guidance_note: Name a rollup after what its source function counts; check whether Progress() counts direct children or descendants before relabeling it.

evidence: printIssueSummary uses formatIssueState(issue), which adds archived/deleted markers, while the new group line prints issue.State() directly, so archived and deleted references look active. Unanswered because the PR merged before the review landed.
guidance_note: When rendering issue state in a new place, reuse the existing formatter that other outputs use.

narrative: A three-minute PR merged about 80 seconds before Copilot's review posted. Both findings, a misleading rollup label and missing archived/deleted markers, are real and remain unaddressed in the packet.
guidance_observations: Merging before the requested review arrives turns real findings into orphaned threads.

evidence: runImportTree had no fs.NArg() check, so extra positional arguments were silently ignored; the agent notes every other no-positional command has the check. Added in 4d353f6.
guidance_note: When adding a CLI subcommand, copy the full argument-validation block from a sibling command, including the NArg check.

evidence: The runImportTree doc said 'creates issues atomically', but Store.ImportTree documents best-effort rollback. Reworded in 4d353f6 to match the store docstring.
guidance_note: Write a wrapper's doc comment from the callee's documented guarantee rather than from the intended one.

evidence: The comment claimed IDs 'always carry the links- prefix', but the prefix is set per workspace through EnsureIssuePrefix. The comment now refers to a generic <prefix>-<n>.

RankSetValidateIDs was exported but its only caller is RankSet in the same file, as the agent confirmed by grep; it was renamed to the unexported rankSetValidateIDs. The hunk also shows RankSet's doc comment sitting on the validator, which the thread did not mention.
guidance_note: Export a helper only when there is a caller outside the package.

evidence: local_id was trimmed only for the emptiness check, and the untrimmed value was used for matching, so stray whitespace caused confusing 'missing parent' errors. The agent chose the reviewer's first option, rejecting surrounding whitespace on local_id, parent and depends_on, rather than silently trimming.
guidance_note: When validating a field with TrimSpace, use the same canonical form everywhere that field is later compared.

narrative: Ergonomics epic bundle. Five accurate, low-severity findings, all fixed together in 4d353f6 with sensible choices where the reviewer offered options.

evidence: The flagged code came from the unmerged feat/field-history-jbn ancestor that the branch was accidentally based on; rebasing onto master removed it from the PR. The agent says 'the concern is real but belongs on whatever PR lands the field-history work', but the packet shows no ticket or comment carrying it there.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, check git log master..HEAD for commits that do not belong to it.

evidence: Export kept Version: 1 while the shape changed from History to Events, so old exports would import with history silently dropped. This is real, but the code was rebased out of this PR; the packet does not show the concern being forwarded to the field-history work.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, check git log master..HEAD for commits that do not belong to it.

evidence: The 24h-to-6h orphan threshold change in gatherReadyAnnotated was part of the accidental ancestor commits and is outdated after the rebase. The agent says the design doc names the event-based liveness cutover as phase-1 follow-up work.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, check git log master..HEAD for commits that do not belong to it.

evidence: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS issue_history discards existing audit rows without a backfill, which is real data loss on upgrade. It was rebased out of this PR, and the packet shows no record forwarding it to the field-history PR where it still applies.
guidance_note: When rebasing out code that drew valid findings, file or link those findings on the branch that still carries the code.

evidence: The PR said 'design doc only' while the diff carried schema and CLI changes. The agent made the description true by rebasing the code out rather than rewriting the description to cover the extra scope.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, compare the diff's file list against the PR description.

evidence: The doc cites cli.go:1134 and ready_state.go:111, line numbers that drift. fbf739d replaced them with symbol names.
guidance_note: In design docs, reference code by symbol name rather than file:line.

evidence: The comment says an empty diff still emits an event, while the reviewer says the code skips recordEvent when len(changes)==0. This was ancestor code rebased out of the PR; the packet shows no forwarding of the drift to the field-history branch.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, check git log master..HEAD for commits that do not belong to it.

evidence: The issue_event_changes query in the hunk has no ORDER BY, so Changes order is nondeterministic. This was ancestor code rebased out; it is not shown being carried to the field-history PR.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, check git log master..HEAD for commits that do not belong to it.

narrative: A design-doc PR accidentally based on an unmerged field-history branch, so Copilot reviewed that branch's schema and CLI code. The agent rebased to doc-only and resolved six code threads as out of scope while calling several of them real; nothing in the packet shows those concerns reaching the field-history branch.
guidance_observations: Verifying the branch base before pushing would have avoided seven of eight findings.
Valid findings resolved as 'belongs elsewhere' need a ticket or link where they belong, or they are lost.
